nahhas-irab:100-100.t: وَعَرَضْنا جَهَنَّمَ: that is, We brought it forth.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: الَّذِينَ كانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ: in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), as a naʿt (adjective) of «the disbelievers» (للكافرين). فِي غِطاءٍ عَنْ ذِكْرِي: that is, they are like one whose eye is covered, so he does not look at the proofs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nor listen to His admonition. وَكانُوا لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعاً: that is, that is burdensome to them.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا عِبادِي مِنْ دُونِي أَوْلِياءَ: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] construes it as meaning «Do they then think that this will benefit them?» Someone else said: there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: «Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors besides Me and I will not punish them?»

nahhas-irab:103-103.t: قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُمْ: Ḥamza differed in this, and Ḥamza's reading is more correct and preferable here. This is the view of Sībawayh, because he considers it far-fetched for the lām to be assimilated into the nūn, and he argued for this with what is considered sound and good; he said: because [the nūn] is not assimilated into the lām, they were averse to assimilating [the lām] into it; yet that is permissible, though remote, in his view, because the two points of articulation are close. «[Translator's note: the text appears defective here: the readings being contrasted (the assimilation of the lām of هل into the nūn, "hen-nunabbiʾukum", versus its pronunciation) are not stated; it is translated as written.]» بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمالًا: accusative as tamyīz (specification).

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ: in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a naʿt (adjective) of «the greatest losers» (للأخسرين); it may be in the position of the nominative, meaning «they are» (هم), and it may be in the position of the accusative, meaning «I mean» (أعني).

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: قُلْ لَوْ كانَ الْبَحْرُ مِداداً لِكَلِماتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ الْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْفَدَ كَلِماتُ رَبِّي: It was said that the meaning is: for what He is able to speak; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best what He intended.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: قُلْ إِنَّما أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ: that is, I am not able to compel you or to force you into what I call you to. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: one says حال من المكان يحول حولا when one moves away from it, and similar among maṣdars (verbal nouns) are عظم عظما and صغر صغرا. «[Translator's note: this remark concerns the word حِوَلًا of verse 108 (لا يبغون عنها حولا), but it stands here in the source.]» فَلْيَعْمَلْ: the original form is فَلِيَعْمَلْ; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness and because the lām has become joined to the fāʾ. وَلا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَداً: It is related from Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās: this concerns the polytheists specifically. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to this view the implied meaning is: «and let him not associate anyone with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so as to worship him alongside Him».

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: وَتَرَكْنا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِي بَعْضٍ: that is, We left them alone and did not hold them back, until they surged among the people.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Akhfash Saʿīd, al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd claimed that at the beginning of this sūra there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), and that the meaning is: Praise be to Allah who sent down the Book to His servant, upright, and did not place any crookedness in it.
(قَيِّماً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The saying of al-Ḍaḥḥāk about it is good: that the meaning is straight, that is, straight in wisdom, with no error in it, no corruption and no contradiction. (عِوَجاً) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). One says «عِوَج» of religion, of a matter and of a road, and «عَوَج» of a piece of wood and a stick, that is, a defect; that is, it is not contradictory.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (إِذْ أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ): that is, fleeing with their religion. (فَقالُوا رَبَّنا آتِنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً): that is, give us from Yourself a mercy by which You save us from these disbelievers; (وَهَيِّئْ لَنا مِنْ أَمْرِنا رَشَداً): that is, (guidance) to what will save us. One says «رُشْد» and «رَشَد», but «رَشَدا» is preferable here so that the verse endings agree.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (فَضَرَبْنا عَلَى آذانِهِمْ): the singular is «أُذُن», feminine; the ḍamma may be dropped because of its heaviness, so you say «أُذْن». (سِنِينَ) is a ẓarf (adverbial of time); one also says «سنينًا», putting the case ending on the nūn. (عَدَداً) is accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «سنين», meaning, according to al-Farrāʾ, "counted", and according to the Basrans, "of number".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
(ثُمَّ بَعَثْناهُمْ لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصى لِما لَبِثُوا أَمَداً) (12). (ثُمَّ بَعَثْناهُمْ): that is, We woke them from their sleep, so that We might know (أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصى). Allah already knew that; among the best of what has been said about it is that its meaning is to make (them) stand to account, as you say to one who brings something false: "Bring your proof and make it clear so that I may know that you are truthful." It was also said: this is knowledge of what is witnessed. The two parties are the people of the Cave, and the people who were alive at the time the people of the Cave were raised. (أَيُّ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أَحْصى) is its khabar (predicate).
(أَمَداً) is accusative, according to al-Farrāʾ, in two ways: one of them as specification (tafsīr), and the other by «لبثهم», that is, by their remaining a period. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first way is preferable, because the meaning is (based) on it. If someone says:
How is separating between «أحصى» and «أمدا» permissible, when your saying «مرّ بنا عشرون اليوم رجلا» is ugly? The answer is that this is stronger than «عشرين» because it carries the meaning of the verb.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (الْفِتْيَةُ) is the plural of «فتى» for a small number, and it is not used as a basis for analogy; (the plural for) a large number is «فتيان».

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: (وَرَبَطْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ): that is, We strengthened them, so that they said before the disbelievers: (رَبُّنا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَنْ نَدْعُوَا مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلهاً لَقَدْ قُلْنا إِذاً شَطَطاً): a maṣdar (verbal noun), and its full form is "a saying of excess"; it may also be an object of the saying.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
(وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ): the implied sense is: remember when you withdrew from them. This is what some of the youths said to others. (وَما يَعْبُدُونَ) is in the position of the accusative, that is, and you withdrew from what they worship and did not worship it, (إِلَّا اللَّهَ): an exception. (فَأْوُوا إِلَى الْكَهْفِ يَنْشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ): the response to the imperative. (وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِرفَقاً): al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that he knew in the speech of the Arabs only «مِرفَق» with kasra on the mīm, for affairs, for the arm and for everything.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ claimed that the eloquent usage is kasra on the mīm, and that fatḥa is permissible. Al-Farrāʾ said:
It is as if those who used fatḥa wanted to distinguish it from the elbow of a person; and both may take fatḥa. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd claimed that there are three good dialectal forms in it: «مِرْفَق», «مَرْفِق» and «مَرْفَق». Whoever says «مِرْفَق» makes it among the things that are moved about and used, like «مِقْطَع»; whoever says «مَرْفِق» makes it like «مَسْجِد», because it is from «رفق يرفق» like «سجد يسجد»; and whoever says «مَرْفَق» makes it mean al-rifq (gentleness). [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing the three forms is not marked in the source; it is supplied here according to the explanations given.]

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: The people of the two Sanctuaries and Abū ʿAmr read (وَتَرَى الشَّمْسَ إِذا طَلَعَتْ تَتَزاوَرُ عَنْ كَهْفِهِمْ) [Translator's note: as printed; by the explanation that follows their reading is «تَزّاوَرُ»], assimilating the tāʾ into the zāy, the root form being «تتزاور». The people of Kufa read «تزاور», omitting the tāʾ. Qatāda, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Ibn ʿĀmir read «تزورّ», like «تحمرّ», and al-Farrāʾ reported «تزوارّ», like «تحمارّ».

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
(ذاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَذاتَ الشِّمالِ): two adverbials (ẓarf). (فِراراً) and (رُعْباً) are both accusative as tamyīz (specification), and according to neither Sībawayh nor al-Farrāʾ may they be placed first; Muḥammad ibn Yazīd permitted that because the governing word is a fully inflected (verb). It is narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash that they read (لَوُ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ) with ḍamma on the wāw.
This is permissible because the ḍamma is of the same kind as the wāw, though the kasra is better. This is not like (أَوِ انْقُصْ) [al-Muzzammil: 3], because after the wāw here there is a ḍamma. (فِراراً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of «ولّيت» is «فررت» (you fled).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: (لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً مِنْ لَدُنْهُ): accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay). The implied sense is: to warn you of severity, that is, punishment from Him.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (وَيُنْذِرَ) is conjoined to it. (الَّذِينَ) are objects. [Translator's note: the source's «مفعولون» is presumably meant as "an object".]

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً): accusative by way of clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)), that is, their statement is grievous: (اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً). «كلمة» is a piece of speech. Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read (كبرت كلمةٌ) in the nominative, by its verb (as fāʿil (agent)), that is, their word is grievous, and it is their saying: Allah has taken a son.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (فَلَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ عَلى آثارِهِمْ): plural of «أَثَر», and one also says «إِثْر». (إِنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَسَفاً): Abū Isḥāq said: «أسفا» is accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). «أسف» is said when one grieves and when one is angry.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t:
(إِنَّا جَعَلْنا ما عَلَى الْأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَها): it was said that «ما» and «زينة» are two objects, and there are two interpretations of it:
one of them is that it is specific to trees, fruit, wealth and the like; the other is that it is general, because it points to its Creator. Another view is that «جعلنا» here means "We created", transitive to «ما», and «زينة» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); this is a good view. (لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ): that is, to test them, so We command them to obey in order to see (أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا); the one good in deeds is the one who renounces adornment. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He will annihilate all of that, so He the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّا لَجاعِلُونَ ما عَلَيْها صَعِيداً جُرُزاً) (8).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: (أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحابَ الْكَهْفِ وَالرَّقِيمِ): that is, "or rather, did you think" that they (كانُوا مِنْ آياتِنا عَجَباً)? Among the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that you see there is what is more wondrous than they. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Quraysh sent al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ from Mecca to Medina to ask the Jewish rabbis about the Prophet ﷺ. They asked them, and they said: Ask him about some youths who went away in the first age and had a wondrous story; about a man who travelled widely and reached the easts and the wests; and about the spirit. If he informs you about the two, he is a prophet; and if he informs you about the spirit, he is not a prophet. So Sūrat al-Kahf was revealed.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
(وَكَذلِكَ بَعَثْناهُمْ): that is, We woke them, (لِيَتَسائَلُوا بَيْنَهُمْ): that is, so that they might ask one another. (قالَ قائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ): «لبتّم» is also permissible, by assimilation, because of the nearness of the two points of articulation. (قالُوا لَبِثْنا يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ): Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: one of them said: We remained a day; another said: We remained about that; so their eldest said to them: Do not disagree, for disagreement is ruin. (رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِما لَبِثْتُمْ). The people of Medina read (فَابْعَثُوا أَحَدَكُمْ بِوَرِقِكُمْ) and assimilated; Ibn Kathīr assimilated the qāf into the kāf because of their closeness. The people of Kufa and Abū ʿAmr read (بِوَرْقِكُمْ), dropping the kasra because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: the source prints both readings in the standard vowelling; the distinction is as described.] Al-Farrāʾ reported that one says «بِوِرْقكم» with kasra on the wāw, as one says «كِبْد» and «فِخْذ». Someone else reported that for al-wariq (silver coin) one says:
«رِقة», like «عِدة»; this is according to the dialect of those who say «وِرْقة» and then drop the wāw, saying «رِقة».
(فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّها أَزْكى طَعاماً فَلْيَأْتِكُمْ): the implied sense is: which of its people. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: He means: which of them has the purest food, because they used to slaughter swine; (so let him bring you provision from it). Kasra on the lām is permissible, and it is the root form; likewise (وَلْيَتَلَطَّفْ).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
(إِنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ يَرْجُمُوكُمْ):
protasis and apodosis (sharṭ and mujāzāt). (أَوْ يُعِيدُوكُمْ) is conjoined to the apodosis. In (إِذاً) there is the meaning of condition and requital. (أَبَداً) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: (إِذْ يَتَنازَعُونَ) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān), and what governs it is «ليعلموا»: when We raised them. [Translator's note: the source's wording «ليعلموا إذ بعثناهم» is elliptical.]

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: (سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلاثَةٌ): with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, they are three. (رابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); likewise (سادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ) and (وَثامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ). Concerning the use of the wāw in «وثامنهم» specifically and not in what precedes, there are two views. One of them is that its presence and its absence are the same; the other is that its presence indicates the completion of the story and the end of the speech. Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī mentioned this view, and the meaning according to it is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reported what they say and then brought the truth of the matter, saying: (وثامنهم كلبهم). (ما يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ): nominative by its verb, that is, few know them.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (غَداً) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān), and its root form is «غدو».

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ) is accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
(وَلَبِثُوا فِي كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلاثَ مِائَةٍ سِنِينَ): this is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The people of Kufa, except ʿĀṣim, read (ثَلاثَ مِائَةِ سِنِينَ) without tanwīn. [Translator's note: the source prints both with the standard vowelling; the distinction is the tanwīn as stated.] In the first reading «سنين» is in the position of the accusative or the genitive. The accusative is as a badal (substitute) for «ثلاث». Abū Isḥāq said: «سنين» is in the position of the accusative as ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) and tawkīd (emphasis). Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ
and Abū ʿUbayda said: The implied sense is: and they remained in their cave years, three hundred. Abū Jaʿfar said: The genitive refers back to «مائة», because it has the meaning of «مئين» (hundreds), as the grammarians recited [al-Kāmil metre], 273:
فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا كخافية الغراب الأسحم
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the hidden wing-feathers of the jet-black raven.)
So he described «حلوبة» (singular) by «سود» (plural) because it has the meaning of the plural. As for «ثلاث مائة سنين» (with the genitive construct), it is far-fetched in Arabic.
One must guard against reading it, because the speech of the Arabs is «ثلاث مائة سنة»; «سنة» has the meaning of «سنين», so you brought it according to the meaning and the root form.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
(أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ): the case ending is removed from it because it is in the form of the imperative, and it has the meaning of exclamation (taʿajjub), that is, how well He hears and how well He sees!
Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, Mālik ibn Dīnār and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read (وَلا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَداةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ) [al-Anʿām: 52], and their argument is that it is written in the codex with a wāw. [Translator's note: as printed; the discussion concerns their reading «بالغُدوة» in al-Kahf: 28, and the source quotes the parallel verse of al-Anʿām in the standard form.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not follow, since they write «الصلاة» and «الحياة» with a wāw. And the Arabs hardly ever say
«الغدوة», because it is definite, and the alif and lām do not enter on a definite noun. It is narrated from al-Ḥasan (لا تعد عينيك), accusative by the action of the verb falling on it.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): concerning the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» there are three views. One of them is that the implied sense is: We do not let the reward of whoever among them does good deeds be lost; then «منهم» was omitted, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has informed us that He nullifies the deeds of the disbelievers. It was also said: the implied sense is: We do not let their reward be lost, because "whoever does good deeds" refers to them. The third answer is that the implied sense is: Those who believe and do righteous deeds — for them are the Gardens of ʿAdn. (عَمَلًا) is accusative by way of clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
(يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها): al-Farrāʾ reported (يَحْلَوْنَ فِيها) [Translator's note: the source prints the standard form; the variant reported is presumably «يَحْلَوْن», given the explanation that follows]. One says «حليت المرأة تحلى فهي حالية» when she wears jewellery, and one says «حلي الشيء يحلى». (مِنْ أَساوِرَ) is in the position of the accusative because it is the predicate of that whose agent is not named (i.e. the second object of the passive verb). (مِنْ ذَهَبٍ) is in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification); however, the most eloquent usage in the speech of the Arabs, when the thing is vague, is to bring «من», and the Qur'an only uses the most eloquent of usages. So one says: «عنده جبّة من خز» and «جبّتان خزّا», and «أساور من ذهب» and «سواران ذهبا». «أساور» is the plural of «أسورة», and «أسورة» is the plural of «سِوار»; one also says «سُوار», and Quṭrub reported «إسوار». Abū Jaʿfar said: Quṭrub is a man of anomalies.
Yaʿqūb and others left him aside and did not mention him. (وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِياباً خُضْراً مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ): if it were «سندسا» it would be permissible, but it is vague, and the eloquent usage is to bring «من» with it, as stated above. Al-Kisāʾī said: the singular of «السندس» is «سندسة», the singular of «العبقريّ» is «عبقريّة», the singular of «الرّفرف» is «رفرفة», and the singular of «الأرائك» is «أريكة». (نِعْمَ الثَّوابُ): nominative by «نعم»; if it were «نعمت» it would be permissible, because it refers to the Garden, and on this basis is (وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً).

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ): the implied form is: a parable, the parable of two men.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
(كِلْتَا الْجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَها): construed according to the form (lafẓ) of «كلتا». Outside the Qur'an the grammarians permitted construing according to the meaning, so that you say «كلتا الجنتين آتتا أكلهما», because the meaning is: the two gardens, both of them brought forth their fruit. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «كلتا الجنتين آتى أكله»; he said: because the meaning is the fruit of the two gardens, or all of the two gardens. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (كلّ الجنتين أتى أكله). The meaning according to al-Farrāʾ on this basis is: everything of the fruit of the two gardens brought forth its produce. He said: Some of the Arabs use the singular of «كلتا» while meaning the dual, and he recited [al-Rajaz metre], 274:
في كلت رجليها سلامي واحده
(In each of her two legs is a single small bone.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them, say «جاءني كلا الرجلين», «رأيت كلا الرجلين» and «مررت بكلا الرجلين», all with an alif in pronunciation. Others said: except that it is written (with yāʾ) in the position of the genitive and the accusative, because one says «رأيت كليهما» and «مررت بكليهما».

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (وَكانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ): al-Akhfash said: and one of the two had.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: The people of Medina read (لأجدنّ خيرا مّنهما منقلبا) with the dual in «منهما», and the people of Kufa read (مِنْها). The dual is preferable because the pronoun is nearer to the two gardens.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (لكِنَّا): the doctrine of al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Māzinī is that the root form is «لكن أنا»; the vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the nūn of «لكن», the hamza was omitted, and the nūn was assimilated into the nūn. The pause on it is «لكنّا», and it is the alif of «أنا», for making the vowel clear; some of the Arabs say «أنه». Abū Ḥātim said: They narrated from ʿĀṣim (لكنّنا هو الله ربّي) [Translator's note: as printed], and he claimed this is a solecism, meaning keeping the alif in continuous recitation. He said: Like it is the reading of whoever read (كِتابِيَهْ) [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] keeping the hāʾ in continuous recitation. Abū Isḥāq said: Keeping the alif in (لكِنَّا هُوَ اللَّهُ رَبِّي) in continuous recitation is good, because the alif has been omitted from «أنا», so they brought it as a compensation. He said: In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is (لكن أنا هو الله ربّي).

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (وَلَوْلا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ ما شاءَ اللَّهُ): in the position of the nominative, and the implied sense is «إلّا من شاء» [Translator's note: as printed; the usual explanation is "it is what Allah wills" (الأمر ما شاء الله)]. The grammarians also permit «ما» to be in the position of the accusative and to be conditional, the implied sense being: whatever Allah wills will be; so the apodosis was omitted. Like it is (فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي السَّماءِ) [al-Anʿām: 35]. (لا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ) is with the lā of generic negation [Translator's note: the source has «على التجربة», most likely a misprint for «على التبرئة», i.e. lā of generic negation], and (لا قوّةٌ إلّا بالله) is also permissible [Translator's note: the source prints it unvowelled; the nominative is presumably meant]. (إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مالًا وَوَلَداً): (أَنَا) is a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position in i'rab; it may also be in the position of the accusative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the nūn and yāʾ. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (إن ترني أنا أقلُّ منك مالا) in the nominative, making «أنا» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أقل» its khabar (predicate), the clause being in the position of the second object; the first object is the nūn and yāʾ, except that the yāʾ was omitted because the kasra indicates it. Keeping it is good and fully correct, and it is the root form, and because it is the real noun (pronoun), whereas the nūn was brought only for a reason.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
(أَوْ يُصْبِحَ ماؤُها غَوْراً): the implied form is «ذا غور» (having sunk away), like (واسأل القرية). Al-Kisāʾī said: One says:
«مياه غور», and «غار الماء يغور غوورا»; with hamza (غؤورا) is also permissible because of the ḍamma on the wāw, and «غورا».

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ): the noun of that whose agent is not named (the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)) is implied, and it is the maṣdar; it is also possible that the genitive (noun) is in the position of the nominative. (فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ) is in the position of the accusative, that is, turning over (his hands).

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
(وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ فِئَةٌ): (فِئَةٌ) is the noun of «تكن», and the khabar (predicate) is (لَهُ); it is also possible that (يَنْصُرُونَهُ) is the khabar.
The first way is preferable according to Sībawayh because «له» has been placed first. Abū al-ʿAbbās disagrees with him and argues from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ) [al-Ikhlāṣ: 4]. Sībawayh permitted the other way, and recited [al-Rajaz metre], 275:
لتقربنّ قربا جلذيّا ... ما دام فيهنّ فصيل حيّا
(You will surely travel to water at a hard, steady pace, as long as there is a weaned young camel alive among them.)
«ينصرونه» is according to the meaning of «فئة», because its meaning is groups of people; if it were according to the form it would be «ولم تكن له فئة تنصره», as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) [Āl ʿImrān: 13]. (وَما كانَ مُنْتَصِراً): that is, nor was he able to help himself either.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: (هُنالِكَ): it was said that this is the completion (of the preceding), so that what governs it is «منتصرا». Better than this is that «هنالك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, in that situation Allah's support, Mighty and Majestic, for His friend becomes clear. The Kufans read «الوِلاية», that is, authority, and that is very far-fetched. In «الحقّ» there are three ways: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «الحقُّ» in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «الولاية»; the people of Medina and Ḥamza read (الْحَقِّ) in the genitive as a naʿt of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the Possessor of truth. Abū Isḥāq said: The accusative is also permissible, as a maṣdar and for emphasis, as one says «هذا لك حقا». (هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَواباً) is by way of clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)). In «عقب» there are three ways: ḍamma on the ʿayn and the qāf; the people of Kufa read (عُقْباً) with ḍamma on the ʿayn, the qāf vowelless, and tanwīn; and Abū Isḥāq said: «عقبى» is also permissible, like «بشرى».

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
In (تَذْرُوهُ) there are three ways: (تَذْرُوهُ) is the reading of the generality. Al-Kisāʾī said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «تذريه»; al-Kisāʾī also reported «تُذريه». [Translator's note: the source does not mark the vowelling distinguishing these two forms.] Al-Farrāʾ reported: «أذريت الرجل عن البعير», that is, I turned him over (threw him off). Sībawayh and al-Mufaḍḍal recited [al-Ṭawīl metre], 276:
فقلت له: صوّب ولا تجهدنّه ... فتذرك من أخرى القطاة فتزلق
(I said to him: Go downhill and do not overtax it, lest it throw you from the back of its rump and you slip off.)
(وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقْتَدِراً): this is among the difficult (passages), and the scholars have discussed it. Some said: «كان» means «يكون»; others said: «كان» means «ما زال». Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq reject that the past could have the meaning of the future except with a particle indicating that. He said: The Arabs were only addressed according to what they know, and they do not know this in their speech. The best of what has been said about this is the view of Sībawayh.
He said: The people witnessed the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it was said to them: thus He has been, that is, He has never ceased to be all-powerful.

nahhas-irab:47-49.t:
(وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبالَ): that is, and remember. Some grammarians said: the implied sense is: and the lasting righteous deeds are better on the day We set the mountains in motion. Abū Jaʿfar said: That is a mistake because of the wāw. (وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بارِزَةً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); likewise (عُرِضُوا عَلى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا);
likewise (لا يُغادِرُ) is in the position of a ḥāl, and likewise (حاضِراً).

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: (فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ): an exception. Abū Isḥāq claimed that it is an exception not of the same kind as the first (i.e. disjoined), because Iblīs was not one of the angels; but he was commanded to prostrate along with them, so he was excepted from them.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Jaʿfar and al-Jaḥdarī read (وَما كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُداً) with fatḥa on the tāʾ [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «كُنْتُ»; their reading is «كُنْتَ»]. In «عضد» there are six forms: the most eloquent is «عَضُد»; the dialect of Banū Tamīm is «عَضْد»; it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he read «عُضُدا» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the ḍād; Hārūn the reader reported «عَضَد». Abū Isḥāq said: «عُضْد» is also permissible; and the sixth dialectal form is «عَضِد», according to the dialect of those who say «فَخِذ» and «كَتِف». [Translator's note: the source does not mark the vowelling of the forms; it is supplied here from the standard lists.] It was said that the pronoun in (ما أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ) refers back to Iblīs and his offspring, and the meaning is: I did not make Iblīs and his offspring witness the creation of the heavens and the earth so that I might seek their help, nor did I make them witness the creation of themselves.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: (وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نادُوا شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ): that is, those whom you made partners in divinity and worship; so call them, so that they may rescue you from the punishment you are in and reward you for your worshipping them.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
(وَرَأَى الْمُجْرِمُونَ النَّارَ): the root form is «رأي»; the yāʾ was changed into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa. For this reason the Kufans claimed that «رأى» is written with yāʾ, and some Basrans followed them in this. As for the skilled Basrans, among them Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, all of this is written in their view with alif. Abū Jaʿfar said:
I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: It is not permissible to write «مضى», «رمى» and everything that has yāʾ (as its final radical) except with alif. There is no difference between those with yāʾ and those with wāw in writing, just as there is no difference between them in pronunciation; writing is only a transfer of what is in pronunciation, just as what is in pronunciation is a transfer of what is in the heart. Whoever writes any of these with yāʾ has caused confusion and produced what is not permissible. If those with yāʾ had to be written with yāʾ, those with wāw would have to be written with wāw. Moreover, they contradict themselves: they write «رمى» with yāʾ and «رماه» with alif; if the reason were that it has yāʾ (as a radical), they would have to write «رماه» with yāʾ. Then they write «ضحا» and «كسا» (plural of «كسوة»), which both have wāw, with yāʾ. This yields nothing and does not hold to any principle. He said: So I said to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: Then why have the scribes and most people followed them in this evident error? He said: The origin of this is al-Akhfash Saʿīd, because he was a man who used stratagems to earn a living, so he used this as a stratagem, and he (the other) is al-Kisāʾī; this is its origin. [Translator's note: the sentence «فاحتال بهذا وهو الكسائي» is elliptical in the source.] Sībawayh reported that one says «راء» (he saw), O you, by transposition. (وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا عَنْها مَصْرِفاً): «مَصْرَفا» is also permissible, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and kasra on the rāʾ as a noun of place. The meaning is: they will not find a place to which they can turn away.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: The first «أن» is in the position of the accusative and the second is in the position of the nominative. The practice of the former peoples is extermination. (أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذابُ قُبُلًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The doctrine of al-Farrāʾ is that «قُبُلا» is (the plural of) «قبيل», that is, scattered, one part following another; and in his view it is also possible that the meaning is "face to face". Al-Aʿraj said — and his reading was «قُبُلا» — its meaning is "all together". Abū ʿAmr said — and his reading was «قِبَلا» — its meaning is "face to face". [Translator's note: the source does not mark the vowelling of these readings; it is supplied according to the standard reports.] Abū Jaʿfar said: This is figurative (majāz): since the proofs had come to them, and what they ought to believe in and ought to accept, they were as though what prevented them from believing was one of these two things.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: (وَما نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ): ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ): that is, (to himself) (مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآياتِ رَبِّهِ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْها): that is, from accepting them, (وَنَسِيَ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ): he neglected his disbelief and his acts of disobedience and did not repent of them.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
(وَتِلْكَ) is in the position of the nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الْقُرى) is a naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute). (أَهْلَكْناهُمْ) is in the position of the khabar (predicate), construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is the people of the towns. It is also possible that «تلك» is in the position of the accusative according to those who say «زيدا ضربته». (وَجَعَلْنا لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ مَوْعِداً): it was said:
the meaning is that it was said to them: if they do not believe, I will destroy them at such-and-such a time, and the destruction of those who were destroyed. ʿĀṣim read «مَهْلَكهم» with fatḥa on the mīm and the lām, and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «هلك». Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted (لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ) with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām. Al-Kisāʾī said: It is dearer to me because it is from «يهلِك». Abū Isḥāq said:
«مهلِك» is a noun of time, and the implied sense is: for the time of their destruction, as one says: «أتت الناقة على مضربها» (the she-camel reached the time of her covering).

nahhas-irab:60-60.t:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِفَتاهُ): and he is Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn. Al-Farrāʾ said: Everyone who takes from someone and learns from him is his "fatā" (young man/attendant), even if he is an old man; he is likened to a servant. (أَوْ أَمْضِيَ حُقُباً): a ẓarf (adverbial). Al-Farrāʾ said:
al-ḥuqub in the dialect of Qays is a year, and in the exegesis it is eighty years. Abū Jaʿfar said: The true sense of al-ḥuqub is a vague period of time, which may be specified as a year, or less or more.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
(فَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ سَرَباً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by «اتّخذ», as you say «هو يدعه تركا» (he leaves it, a leaving).
It may also be a second object, as one says «اتّخذت زيدا وكيلا», and like it «اتّخذت مكان كذا وكذا طريقا».

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: (فَلَمَّا جاوَزا): the implied form is: when they had passed the meeting place of the two seas; the object was omitted. (قالَ لِفَتاهُ آتِنا غَداءَنا): two objects. (لَقَدْ لَقِينا مِنْ سَفَرِنا هذا نَصَباً): that is, [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here.]

nahhas-irab:63-63.t:
(فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ): it was said: the meaning is: I forgot to tell you the news of the fish, that it came to life and then slipped into the sea; and he forgot this great sign because signs were plentiful at that time.
(وَما أَنْسانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطانُ): ḍamma on the hāʾ is permissible, according to the root form; keeping the wāw is permissible, and likewise keeping the yāʾ if you use kasra. (أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); the implied sense is: and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan; that is, Satan whispered to him and occupied his heart until he forgot, so the forgetting was attributed to Satan figuratively. (وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ عَجَباً): Abū Isḥāq said:
There are two ways in it: Yūshaʿ, Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: (واتّخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا); and the other way is that Yūshaʿ, peace be upon him, said: (واتّخذ سبيله في البحر), and Mūsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «عجبا», that is, I marvel greatly. [Translator's note: in the source the second way is printed with «عجبا» in both places.] He said: There is a third way in it which is preferable to what Abū Isḥāq said, namely that Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: The meaning is: Mūsā took the path of the fish in the sea and marvelled greatly. [Translator's note: the source has «قال» ("he said") before the third way, though it is evidently Abū Jaʿfar speaking.] Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: Mūsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, followed the trail of the fish, watched its turning about in the water, and marvelled at its disappearing in it.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: (قالَ ذلِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ما كُنَّا نَبْغِ) is its khabar (predicate). The yāʾ was omitted because it is the end of the utterance, so it resembled the verse endings. (فَارْتَدَّا عَلى آثارِهِما قَصَصاً): that is, they went back along the road they had come by, retracing the trail, a retracing.

nahhas-irab:65-66.t: (فَوَجَدا عَبْداً مِنْ عِبادِنا آتَيْناهُ): it may be a naʿt (adjective), and it may be resumptive. (وَعَلَّمْناهُ) is conjoined to it. (مِنْ لَدُنَّا): (لَدُنْ) is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is not fully nominal (lā tatamakkan). (عِلْماً) is a second object. The people of Medina and the people of Kufa read (رُشْداً), and Abū ʿAmr read «رَشَدا»; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t:
(خُبْراً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of «أحطت به» and «خبرته» is one. [Translator's note: the word under discussion, «خبرا», is not quoted in the source.] Like it is [al-Ṭawīl metre], 277:
فسرنا إلى الحسنى ورقّ كلامنا ... ورضت فذلّت صعبة أيّ إذلال
(So we came to fair terms and our speech grew gentle, and I broke in a refractory one, and she was humbled — what a humbling!)
because the meaning of «رضت» is «أذللت».

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: (قالَ فَإِنِ اتَّبَعْتَنِي فَلا تَسْئَلْنِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ): that is, if you see something you find objectionable, do not hasten to ask me about it until I mention it to you.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t:
(قالَ أَخَرَقْتَها لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَها): the people of Kufa, except ʿĀṣim, read (ليغرق أهلُها), and the meaning is the same. (لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئاً إِمْراً): it was said: Mūsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, only said this to him because he did not know that he was a prophet and that this was by revelation. It was also said: It is not possible that Mūsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, accompanied him in order to learn from him unless he was a prophet, because the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, learn only from the angels or from the prophets, Allah bless them and grant them peace. It was only said «لقد جئت شيئا إمرا» and «نكرا», that is, it is outwardly objectionable until we know the wisdom in it.
(شَيْئاً) is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), that is, you have done something; it is also possible that the implied form is «جئت بشيء إمر», then the bāʾ was omitted, so the verb became transitive and put it in the accusative.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: (قالَ لا تُؤاخِذْنِي بِما نَسِيتُ): there are two views on its meaning. One of them is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: This is among the indirect expressions of speech (maʿārīḍ al-kalām). The other is that he forgot, so he apologised, and he did not forget the second time, for if he had forgotten he would have apologised. (وَلا تُرْهِقْنِي مِنْ أَمْرِي عُسْراً): two objects.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t:
(فَانْطَلَقا حَتَّى إِذا لَقِيا غُلاماً فَقَتَلَهُ قالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً زَكِيَّةً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ): the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and Abū ʿAmr (is «زاكية»), and the Kufans read (زَكِيَّةً). [Translator's note: the source prints the standard «زَكِيَّةً» in the verse quotation and does not spell out the first reading; by what follows it is «زاكية».] Abū ʿAmr claimed that «زاكية» is preferable here, because «الزاكية» is the one that has no sin, and the one whom al-Khaḍir, Allah bless him, killed was a small child. Most people disagreed with him in this. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said:
«زاكية» and «زكيّة» are the same. Others said: If the matter were as he said, «زكيّة» would be preferable, because «فعيل» is more intensive than «فاعل». And it is not established that the one whom al-Khaḍir killed was a small child; rather, the apparent sense of the Qur'an indicates that he was an adult. «بغير نفس» indicates that, for it shows that killing him in retaliation for a soul would be permissible, and that is not the case for a child, as retaliation (qawad) applies only after puberty. (نُكْراً) is the root form, and whoever says «نُكْرا» [Translator's note: as printed; presumably the contrast is between «نُكُراً» and «نُكْراً»] has dropped the ḍamma because of its heaviness.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t:
(قالَ إِنْ سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ بَعْدَها): that is, after this question, (قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِنْ لَدُنِّي عُذْراً): that is, on my part; my pushing you away from accompanying me has (become) excusable for you. This is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. The people of Medina read «من لدُني» with the nūn light (undoubled). The first reading is preferable in Arabic and more regular, because the root form is «لدن» with the nūn vowelless; then you add a yāʾ to it to annex it to yourself, then you add a nūn so that the vowellessness of the nūn of «لدن» is preserved, just as we say «عنّي» and «منّي»; so just as you do not say «عني», you should not say «لدني». The argument for its permissibility, according to what is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, is that the nūn was omitted, as the people of Medina read (فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونِ) [al-Ḥijr: 54] with kasra on the nūn. Better than this view is what Abū Isḥāq held. He said: «لدن» is a noun and «عن» is a particle, and omission in nouns is permissible, as he said [al-Rajaz metre], 278:
قدني من نصر الخبيبين قدي
(Enough for me of helping the two Khubaybs — enough for me!)
So he brought both forms together. He said: Moreover, «لدن» is heavier than «عن» and «من».

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read (فأبوا أن يُضِيفوهما), light (undoubled). One says «أضفته» and «ضيّفته», that is, I lodged him as a guest, and «ضفته», that is, I inclined, I stayed with him. [Translator's note: the source has «مالت» ("she inclined"); «ملت» ("I inclined") seems intended.] It is derived from «ضاف السّهم», that is, (the arrow) swerved, and «ضافت الشمس», that is, (the sun) inclined towards setting. And it (al-muḍāf ilayhi) is genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), that is, by the annexing of the noun to it.
It is narrated from Abū ʿAmr and Mujāhid (لَتَخِذْتَ). One says «تخذ يتخذ», and «اتّخذ» is the iftaʿala form of it.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: (قالَ هذا فِراقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ): the repetition of «بين» is, according to Sībawayh, for emphasis, that is, this is the parting of "between us", that is, of our connection. Sībawayh said: Like it is «أخزى الله الكاذب منّي ومنك», that is, of us. Al-Farrāʾ permitted (the accusative) — he said: «هذا فراقٌ بينِي وبينَك» — as an adverbial (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:79-79.t:
(أَمَّا السَّفِينَةُ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (فَكانَتْ لِمَساكِينَ). «مساكين» is a diptote because it is a plural with no counterpart among singulars. (وَكانَ وَراءَهُمْ مَلِكٌ): most of the exegetes say that «وراء» means "in front of". Abū Isḥāq said: This is permissible because «وراء» is derived from «توارى» (to be hidden), so whatever is hidden from you is «وراءك», whether it is in front of you or behind you. According to Abū Isḥāq's view, «وراء» would then necessarily not be of those (words) with hamza (as a radical), and its diminutive would be «وريئة». Al-Farrāʾ claimed that one does not say of a man in front of you: he is «وراءك», nor of a man behind you: he is «بين يديك»; that is only said of times of night and day and of time in general.
One says: «بين يديك برد» (cold is before you), even if it has not yet come to you, and «وراءك برد», even if it is before you, because when it overtakes you it comes to be behind you.

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: (وَأَمَّا الْغُلامُ فَكانَ أَبَواهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ): according to Sībawayh, «مؤمنان» is permissible outside the Qur'an, by implying (a pronoun) in «كان», with «أبواه مؤمنان» as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of «كان». Sībawayh reported: «كلّ مولود يولد على الفطرة حتّى يكون أبواه هما اللذان يهودانه وينصّرانه» (Every child is born upon the natural disposition until his parents are the ones who make him a Jew and make him a Christian). (فَخَشِينا أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُما طُغْياناً وَكُفْراً): that is, transgression in what is not due. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew this of him if He let him live, so He commanded what was best to be done.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
(خَيْراً مِنْهُ زَكاةً وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْماً): most of the exegetes say: al-zakāh is religion, and al-ruḥm is
affection. Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not depart from the language, because al-zakāh is derived from al-zakāʾ, which is growth and increase, and al-ruḥm is from al-raḥma (mercy), as he said [al-Rajaz metre], 279:
يا منزل الرّحم على إدريس ... ومنزل اللّعن على إبليس
(O You who sent down mercy upon Idrīs, and sent down the curse upon Iblīs.)

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: (رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun). (ذلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ ما لَمْ تَسْطِعْ): we will mention it in the next group of ten (verses), because it is more fitting there.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t:
(فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَباً): that is, (one) of the means which he had been given. This is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr [Translator's note: i.e. «فاتَّبع», with connecting hamza and doubled tāʾ; the source prints the standard Kufan form in the quotation].
The reading of the Kufans is «فأتبع», which they made with a disjunctive hamza (alif qaṭʿ); this reading is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because it is (a verb) of travelling. He and al-Aṣmaʿī reported that one says «تبعه» and «اتّبعه» when one travels (after someone) without overtaking him, and «أتبعه» when you overtake him. Abū ʿUbayd said: Like it is (فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ مُشْرِقِينَ) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 60]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This distinction, even though al-Aṣmaʿī reported it, is not accepted except with a reason or proof. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ مُشْرِقِينَ), there is nothing in the report that they overtook them; the report is only that when Mūsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his companions came out of the sea and Pharaoh and his companions were (in it), the sea closed over them. The truth in this is that «تبع», «أتبع» and «اتّبع» are dialectal forms with one meaning, namely travelling (after), which may or may not involve overtaking.

nahhas-irab:86-87.t:
(وَجَدَها تَغْرُبُ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فِي عَيْنٍ): and al-ḥamʾa is mud altered in colour and smell. [Translator's note: the source quotes only «في عين», without «حمئة».] (وَوَجَدَ عِنْدَها قَوْماً قُلْنا يا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّا أَنْ تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْناً): Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned the view of Abū Isḥāq that the meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him the choice between these two rulings. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān rejected his saying that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him the choice: it is not established that Dhū al-Qarnayn was a prophet so as to be addressed with this; and how could he say of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, (ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلى رَبِّهِ), and how could he say (فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ), addressing with the nūn (of the plural)? He said: The implied sense is: We said, O Muḥammad, they said: O Dhū al-Qarnayn. Abū Jaʿfar said: What Abū al-Ḥasan said entails nothing. As for (قُلْنا يا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ), it is possible that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addressed him through the tongue of a prophet in his time; and it is possible that He said this to him just as He said (فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِداءً) [Muḥammad: 4]. As for the difficulty of (فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلى رَبِّهِ), its implied sense is that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him the choice between killing, in His saying (إِمَّا أَنْ تُعَذِّبَ), and sparing, in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (وَإِمَّا أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْناً),
(قالَ) to those people: (أَمَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ), that is, whoever of you persists in disbelief, (فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ), that is, by killing, (ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلى رَبِّهِ), that is, on the Day of Resurrection, (فَيُعَذِّبُهُ عَذاباً نُكْراً), that is, severe.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t:
(وَأَمَّا مَنْ آمَنَ): that is, repented of disbelief, (وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً). Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: «أن» is in the position of the accusative in (إِمَّا أَنْ تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْناً). He said: If he had put it in the nominative it would have been correct, in the sense of «فإمّا هو», as he said [al-Ṭawīl metre], 280:
فسيرا فإمّا حاجة تقضيانها ... وإمّا مقيل صالح وصديق
(So travel on: either a need that you two will fulfil, or a good resting place and a friend.)
(فَلَهُ جَزاءً الْحُسْنى) is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; the rest of the Kufans read (فَلَهُ جَزاءً الْحُسْنى); Ibn Abī Isḥāq read (فله جزاء حسنى); and from Ibn ʿAbbās and Masrūq (فَلَهُ جَزاءً الْحُسْنى), accusative without tanwīn. [Translator's note: the source prints the first, second and fourth readings in the same form; by the discussion that follows they are «جزاءُ الحسنى» (nominative, annexed), «جزاءً الحسنى» (accusative with tanwīn) and «جزاءَ الحسنى» (accusative without tanwīn), and the third is presumably «جزاءً حسنى».] Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading has two interpretations. One of them is that «جزاء» is nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject) or by the (implied verb of) settling (istiqrār), and «الحسنى» is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), the tanwīn being dropped for the annexation. The other interpretation is that the tanwīn is dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and «الحسنى» is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) according to the Basrans, and as a "translation" (tarjama) according to the Kufans. The second reading is on this (latter) basis, except that you have not dropped the tanwīn, and that is better.
The third reading has three views: al-Farrāʾ said: «جزاء» is accusative as tamyīz (specification); the second view is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); and Abū Isḥāq said: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, being requited with it, a requital. The fourth reading, according to Abū Ḥātim, is with the tanwīn dropped, and it is like the second; according to others this is a mistake, because it is not a place for dropping the tanwīn due to the meeting of two vowelless letters, so its implied sense would be: for him is the reward, as a requital of the best. And «عندها» means «عند العين» (near the spring).

nahhas-irab:89-90.t: (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَباً حَتَّى إِذا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ الشَّمْسِ): one also says «مطلَع», and it is the regular (analogical) form. [Translator's note: the source does not mark the vowelling; «مطلِع» and «مطلَع» are presumably meant.]

nahhas-irab:91-92.t: (كَذلِكَ) has the meaning of «الأمر كذلك» (the matter is thus); it is also possible that the kāf is in the position of the accusative, that is, it rises a rising like that. (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَباً. حَتَّى إِذا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ) is the reading of the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim; the people of Mecca and Abū ʿAmr read (بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ), and the one after it likewise; the Kufans, except ʿĀṣim, read this one with ḍamma and the one after it with fatḥa. [Translator's note: the source prints the readings without distinguishing the vowelling; in the standard reports the Medinans and ʿĀṣim read «السُّدَّيْن» and Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr «السَّدَّيْن».] People have discussed «السُّدّ» and «السَّدّ». ʿIkrima said: Everything that is of the making of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is «سُدّ» with ḍamma, and whatever is of the handiwork of the children of Adam is «سَدّ» with fatḥa. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: «السَّدّ» with fatḥa is the barrier between you and a thing, and «السُّدّ» with ḍamma is a film over the eye. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq said: «السَّدّ» with fatḥa is what your eyes have not seen, and «السُّدّ» with ḍamma is what your eyes have seen. Abū Jaʿfar said: These distinctions are not accepted except with argument and proof, especially since al-Kisāʾī said: They are two dialectal forms with one meaning. This disagreement arose without proof or argument. The truth in this is what is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: he said: «السَّدّ» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) — and this is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — and «السُّدّ» is the noun. If it is thus, the reading with ḍamma is preferable, because what is intended is the noun, not the maṣdar. (وَجَدَ مِنْ دُونِهِما قَوْماً لا يَكادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا) is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; the rest of the Kufans read (يُفْقِهُونَ قَوْلًا) with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and this is with omission of the object, that is, they can hardly make anyone understand speech; the first is without omission. On both readings the meaning is that they neither understand nor make (others) understand.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t: (قالُوا يا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ): in their language, or by gesture. (إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ): ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿraj read (إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ) with hamza [Translator's note: the source prints the same form twice; the first presumably stands for the reading without hamza, «ياجوج وماجوج»], making them derived from «أجيج النار» (the blazing of fire), according to al-Kisāʾī; they would then be Arabic, and they are diptotes because they are made names of two tribes. (فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجاً) is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; the rest of the Kufans read «خراجا». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd holds that «الخرج» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and «الخراج» is the noun, and that the meaning of «استخرجت الخراج» is "I brought it out into the open", and the Day of Emergence is the day of appearing. (عَلى أَنْ تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا): we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: (قالَ ما مَكَّنِّي فِيهِ رَبِّي خَيْرٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), that is, the means with which my Lord has established me, which I have been given, are better than the tribute you would make for me. Mujāhid and Ibn Kathīr read (قال ما مكّنني) without assimilation, because the first nūn is of the verb and the second is not of it; assimilation is good because two letters of the same kind come together. (أَجْعَلْ) is jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the imperative.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: «ساوى» and «سوّى» are the same. Abū Isḥāq said: «الصُّدُفان» and «الصَّدَفان» are the two sides of the mountain. [Translator's note: the vowelling of the two forms is not marked in the source.] The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read (قالَ آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً) in the sense of "give me molten brass, I will pour it"; the reading of the Kufans is «ايتوني», in the sense of "come to me, helping". (آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً): (قِطْراً) is accusative in this reading by «أفرغ».

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: (فَمَا اسْطاعُوا أَنْ يَظْهَرُوهُ): Abū ʿUbayd reported that Ḥamza used to assimilate the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ and double the ṭāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: What Abū ʿUbayd reported, no one is able to pronounce, because the sīn is vowelless and the assimilated ṭāʾ is vowelless. Sībawayh said: this is impossible — assimilating the tāʾ into what follows it — and it is not permissible to vowel the sīn because it is built on vowellessness. There are four dialectal forms in it, reported by Sībawayh, al-Aṣmaʿī and al-Akhfash. One says «استطاع يستطيع»; and «اسطاع يسطيع», dropping the tāʾ because it is from the point of articulation of the ṭāʾ; and one says «استاع يستيع», dropping the ṭāʾ; and the fourth dialectal form is «أسطاع يُسطيع», with a disjunctive hamza and ḍamma on the first letter of the imperfect. Its root according to Sībawayh is «أطاع يطيع», and they brought the sīn as compensation for the loss of the vowel of the ʿayn. Al-Kisāʾī reported «أنت تِستطيع» with kasra on the first tāʾ.

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: (قالَ هذا رَحْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّي): that is, this deed is a favour from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and mercy from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is favour and kindness. (فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّي): that is, the time in which He promised that Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj would come out, (جَعَلَهُ دَكَّاءَ), in the sense of a levelled spot and levelled ground.
